name: liquid-slider

frames.best_why: A clean still with the readout, glass outline, flat water surface and scale all readable and no cursor.

tagline: Fills a glass with blue water as you drag the level up or down.
summary: A vertical water-volume control shaped like a drinking glass. Dragging or using the keys raises and lowers the blue liquid, whose surface ripples and sloshes, with bubbles rising when it is poured quickly.
appearance: A tall rounded card headed "Water today" with a large millilitre readout. Below sits a line-drawn cylindrical glass with a pale elliptical rim, a solid blue body of water, faint bubbles, a white highlight down the left wall and small scale numbers on the right.
behaviour: Dragging up or down chases the water level on a spring, and the surface tilts and ripples under the finger with bubbles rising and popping. Releasing settles it onto the nearest step, and the arrow, page, home and end keys move it too.
demo_content: The label "Water today" showing a value such as 1,250 ml against a scale from 0 to 2,000.
search_phrases: drag to set how much water
use_when: A single level or amount benefits from a tactile, literal liquid metaphor such as water tracking.
avoid_when: The glass is a fixed 280 by 360 drawing with hardcoded geometry, so it cannot stretch or reflow.
customise: Value, default value, range, step, unit, label and a value formatter are props; the glass geometry, colours and wave simulation are fixed in the file.
weight_why: A requestAnimationFrame wave simulation over 34 columns while the liquid moves, idle once settled.

a11y.note: It is a real slider with aria-valuenow, valuetext and a label, full key support, a focus outline, and reduced-motion snaps the level.

issues: The scale numbers on the right of the glass are tiny and low contrast.
polish_why: Distinctive liquid physics and real slider semantics; only the tiny scale text is weak.
